=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves clearly attached at the same node, visible in close-up images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped tightly at the shoot apex)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade without divisions into leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins are smooth without teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (broadest at or near the middle, tapering to both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapering to a sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base is broadly curved)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs from base to apex, with lateral veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, spaced widely, numerous (secondary veins are clearly visible, running from midrib to margin, spaced apart)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): dull (surface appears matte, not glossy)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or fuzz on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is short, leaf blade is sessile or nearly so)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petiole is round in cross-section, not flattened or winged)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears firm and slightly thickened, typical of young woody plant)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem)
    19. Stem color: greenish-brown (stem is dark green to brownish, with some mottling)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface appears smooth without ridges or lenticels)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at leaf base)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no exudate seen when stem or leaf is damaged)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaf base visible)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils observed)

F. Notes: Multiple images show the same seedling from different angles. Leaves exhibit damage including holes and margin irregularities, likely from herbivory or mechanical injury. A pink tag is attached to the stem, likely for research or monitoring purposes. The seedling appears to be growing in a forest floor setting with leaf litter, though specific habitat conditions are not assessed per rules. The whorled leaf arrangement is confirmed by close-up views showing multiple leaves emerging from a single node. Leaf surfaces have some white speckling, possibly mineral deposits or fungal growth, but not clearly identifiable as trichomes.
